next_round_constraints: Keep SEIRS as the primary structure family; deprioritize SEIR and SEIHR unless paired with a clear rationale for improved robustness.
Focus on observation_map = delayed_I; explore delay_weeks in a narrow neighborhood around 2 (e.g., 1–3) rather than broad changes.

Prefer non-fractional (integer-order) dynamics as the baseline; if proposing fractional variants, require improved rolling stability (lower split-to-split variability) rather than only better single validation fit.
Avoid adding extra compartments/observation mixtures (e.g., I+H) unless they demonstrably reduce rolling instability; keep complexity increases minimal.
observed_failure_modes: SEIR/SEIHR structures underperform relative to SEIRS, suggesting missing reinfection/waning-immunity dynamics for this age group’s hospitalization-rate pattern.
Fractional SEIRS with shorter delay shows instability across rolling splits (higher rolling error variability), indicating sensitivity/overflexibility despite good single validation fit.

Direct hospitalization-state observation maps (H or I+H) fit poorly here, implying the observed hospitalization-rate series is better captured as a lagged proxy of infections rather than an explicit H compartment in these templates.

Delay choice matters: delayed_I with ~2-week lag appears more robust than shorter lag in rolling evaluation, consistent with a smoother, lagged relationship between infections and recorded hospitalizations.
